text:
Marcus Reed: Heads up: baseline Run 1 anomaly showing up only in *long-context streaming* shape. Seeing p95 TTFT + tail E2E jump vs last week’s dry run.

Marcus Reed: Affected workload: `lc_stream_chat_8k_out256_conc32_cachecold` (from suite v0). Non-streaming equivalent looks flat.

Marcus Reed: Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-baseline/run-1?var_shape=lc_stream_chat_8k_out256_conc32_cachecold&var_model=llama-70b&var_region=us-east-1

Noah Patel: Is this all regions or just one fleet?

Marcus Reed: So far: only `us-east-1` and only on H100 pool `h100-sxm5-a` (the other pool `h100-pcie-b` is closer to expected but still slightly worse).

Rina Kobayashi: Can you paste the run metadata? commit + runtime build?

Marcus Reed: Runner says:
- runtime: `redwood` `7c2b9d1` (nightly)
- benchmark-lab: `b7a14f2`
- cuda: `12.4`
- driver: `550.54.14`
- shape seed: `104729`

Sofia Ivanova: When you say “TTFT jump” do we know it’s real latency vs instrumentation? streaming TTFT is always tricky.

Grace Kim: +1. Is it TTFT only or also TPOT / throughput?

Marcus Reed: TTFT p95: 1.4s -> 2.9s (ouch). TPOT p95 went from ~32ms/token -> ~34ms/token (small). Throughput overall not down much.

Omar El-Sayed: That pattern smells like queue wait / scheduling under prefill for long prompts, not decode kernels. Any scheduler metrics? queue wait histos?

Marcus Reed: Pulled a sample from the new scheduler counters (thanks Julian):
- `queue_wait_ms_p95`: 820ms (was ~210ms)
- `prefill_batch_tokens_p95`: 62k (was ~40k)
- `prefill_queue_depth_p95`: 11 (was ~4)
Decode metrics look normal-ish.

Julian Moore: That points to prefill getting stuck behind big batches. Did batching heuristics change recently for mixed lengths? There’s a WIP around fairness.

Noah Patel: This is *long-context* though; shouldn’t be mixed.

Sofia Ivanova: Even in “long-context” shape, concurrency means you can end up with some requests at 8k and some at ~6k depending on generator jitter. If the batcher is trying to pack, it might be building whales.

Grace Kim: Can we confirm request distribution? The generator should target 8192 prompt tokens but with tokenizer variance.

Rina Kobayashi: I can re-run with the exact same seed and dump actual prompt token counts per request. If we’re accidentally generating a heavier tail, would explain it.

Marcus Reed: I already checked runner artifact `requests.csv` for one shard. prompt_tokens p50 ~7920, p95 ~8450. That seems within expected.

Hiro Tanaka: If TPOT isn’t moving, kernels likely fine. TTFT moving with queue wait suggests scheduler.

Omar El-Sayed: Another possibility: streaming path “first chunk” flush is delayed (e.g. waiting for N tokens before emitting). If it changed, server-side TTFT could look worse.

Nadia Rahman: Logan/telemetry question: are we measuring TTFT for streaming as “server generated first token” or “first token chunk written to socket”? If it’s the former, we could have backpressure from stream writer.

Logan Wright: Current metric `ttft_ms` is from `request_start` -> `first_token_timestamp` in runtime. For streaming we *try* to use “first chunk enqueued” but there are edge cases when the first chunk is empty / coalesced.

Sofia Ivanova: Wait… do we coalesce for long-prefill? some paths delay the initial chunk until after prefill completes?

Julian Moore: For streaming, we don’t emit until decode starts anyway. But “first token timestamp” is decode start, not “client sees bytes”.

Sean Gallagher: If TTFT is used for baseline, we need a stable definition. But the queue_wait spike suggests this is not purely telemetry. That’s real waiting.

Noah Patel: Can someone paste an example trace/log line for an impacted request?

Marcus Reed: From benchmark runner logs (client side):
```
req_id=8f1b... prompt_tok=8321 out_tok=256 conc=32
client_send_ts=1708446120.118
first_byte_ts=1708446123.071  (TTFT=2.953s)
last_byte_ts=1708446132.884
status=200
```
And server side snippet (from runtime debug sampling):
```
req_id=8f1b... start=... prefill_begin=+74ms prefill_end=+1880ms
queue_wait=+905ms decode_begin=+1902ms first_token=+1910ms
stream_write_first_chunk=+2710ms
```
So even server’s first token is ~1.9s, but client first byte is ~2.95s.

Logan Wright: That last line is key: `stream_write_first_chunk` at +2710ms. That’s huge.

Nadia Rahman: That implies something in streaming writer/flush path is buffering. Maybe chunk threshold? or event-loop starvation?

Sofia Ivanova: But why only long-context? Because prefill is heavy; if stream writer runs on same executor/threadpool, it may be starved.

Omar El-Sayed: Also could be the “first chunk timestamp” instrumentation bug (we’ve seen cases where first chunk is empty and timestamp gets set on second chunk).

Grace Kim: Does the runner consider “first byte” at HTTP level? If runtime sends headers early but no body, some libs won’t call it.

Rina Kobayashi: Runner uses `aiohttp` streaming iterator; TTFT is first chunk of body. If server is sending headers only, we won’t count it.

Julian Moore: Do we have a recent change in streaming chunking? I vaguely remember a refactor around “flush every N tokens”.

Noah Patel: Search recent PRs touching streaming timestamps. I recall something in the 239xx range.

Marcus Reed: Possible suspect: <https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/23944|redwood#23944> ("Fix TTFT instrumentation edge case for streaming responses") — it’s open, not merged yet.

Nadia Rahman: That PR title sounds exactly like this.

Logan Wright: Yep, that PR changes how we pick first-chunk timestamp when the first write is metadata-only / zero-length. Would explain a *measurement* regression, not a real one.

Sean Gallagher: But we also saw queue_wait + prefill_batch_tokens jump. That’s not measurement.

Sofia Ivanova: Two things can be true:
1) Real queue wait increased (scheduler)
2) TTFT is inflated further by stream writer timestamp bug

Omar El-Sayed: +1. Real decode_begin at +1902ms is already worse than baseline expected (~1100-1400ms for this shape).

Hiro Tanaka: Do we have a diff from earlier dry run build? what commit were we comparing against?

Marcus Reed: Dry run last week was runtime `6f8d0a2`.

Noah Patel: Let’s bisect between `6f8d0a2` and `7c2b9d1` with just this shape (maybe 3 trials). That’s small enough.

Rina Kobayashi: I can kick bisection runs on `us-east-1` H100-SXM pool if SRE is ok with capacity.

Sean Gallagher: OK as long as it’s off-peak and pinned fleet label. Use the “benchmark” node pool, not shared.

Julian Moore: For scheduler part: could it be <https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/23981|redwood#23981> (load-shedding hook + fairness tweak)? It touched queueing.

Sofia Ivanova: 23981 changes fairness under bursty workloads; might interact with long prefills at conc=32. But I think it should *reduce* tail, not increase.

Noah Patel: Still worth checking if it accidentally penalizes prefill admission.

Marcus Reed: Another relevant batching PR: <https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24033|redwood#24033> is not in this range yet, so not it.

Grace Kim: Action items?

Marcus Reed: Proposing:
1) Rina runs 3 commits: `6f8d0a2`, mid-point, `7c2b9d1` on the exact shape w/ debug sampling enabled.
2) Logan/Nadia validate TTFT definition for streaming baseline: server first_token vs client first_byte, and whether we should baseline both.
3) Sofia/Julian look at queue_wait change deltas: check batcher config + scheduler counters around prefill queue depth.

Mateo Alvarez: Please also drop a note in the baseline channel summary doc; we can’t lock baselines with an unresolved definition issue on TTFT.

Nadia Rahman: +1. Also: can we add a metric `stream_first_write_ms` separately? That seems directly relevant.

Logan Wright: We already have a draft counter in telemetry branch; I’ll see if I can land it behind a flag, but short-term we can scrape from debug logs.

Rina Kobayashi: Kicking off reruns now. Commands for record:
```
bench run \
  --shape lc_stream_chat_8k_out256_conc32_cachecold \
  --model llama-70b \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --hardware h100-sxm \
  --trials 3 \
  --seed 104729 \
  --runtime-commit 6f8d0a2 \
  --enable-runtime-debug-sampling 0.02
```
Will post artifacts when done.

Sofia Ivanova: I’m going to look specifically at prefill batch construction. If `prefill_batch_tokens_p95` jumped, something changed packing strategy.

Julian Moore: I’ll compare scheduler config defaults between those commits (queueing weights, admission control). Might be a default change.

Marcus Reed: For anyone wanting raw run table: https://drive.redwood.ai/perf/baselines/run-1?shape=lc_stream_chat_8k_out256_conc32_cachecold

Grace Kim: :eyes: on this. If it turns out to be mostly metric definition, we should annotate Run 1 results as “TTFT-streaming suspect” so people don’t panic.

Sean Gallagher: Agreed, but only after we confirm.

Rina Kobayashi: Update (first commit done):
- `6f8d0a2` client TTFT p95: ~1.55s
- server first_token p95: ~1.22s
- client first_byte p95: ~1.60s
queue_wait p95: ~260ms

Rina Kobayashi: `7c2b9d1` currently running; early samples show server first_token p95 ~1.85-1.95s and client first_byte p95 ~2.7-3.0s. So definitely two deltas.

Logan Wright: That widening gap (server first_token -> client first_byte) is consistent with the streaming first-chunk timestamp bug. I’m going to comment on <https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/23944|redwood#23944> that baseline is blocked on it.

Omar El-Sayed: And server first_token got worse too, meaning scheduler/backpressure got worse for long prefill.

Sofia Ivanova: I found a change in batcher default: prefill packing now prefers “maximize tokens” over “maximize request count” when streaming=true (intended to reduce TPOT variance). Might be making whales.

Julian Moore: That’s likely it. If prefill is building massive token batches, queue_wait will balloon at conc=32.

Noah Patel: Can we flip that knob for baseline suite? Or adjust shape to avoid pathological packing?

Sofia Ivanova: I’d rather fix runtime default or make it explicit in baseline config. Baseline should represent real prod defaults, but if defaults are wrong, we should fix.

Mateo Alvarez: Let’s do both:
- For Q1 baseline: lock config explicitly (so suite reproducible)
- For runtime: open a PR to adjust streaming prefill packing to cap batch tokens / improve fairness

Marcus Reed: I’ll file a ticket + link this thread. Also: once 23944 merges, we should rerun this shape before “locking” Run 1 numbers.

Sean Gallagher: Please tag SRE in the rerun plan; we need to note baseline refresh criteria in runbook.

Rina Kobayashi: I’ll post full artifacts once the last trials finish + I’ll add a `diff.md` summary with:
- server_first_token TTFT
- client_first_byte TTFT
- queue_wait histos
- prefill_batch_tokens distribution

Marcus Reed: Thanks all. Tentative conclusion: (a) real scheduler queueing regression for long-prefill streaming due to prefill packing default; (b) additional streaming TTFT measurement inflation due to first-chunk timestamp edge case (pending <https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/23944|redwood#23944>).

Marcus Reed: I’ll update the baseline Run 1 anomaly list with this and mark the shape as “do not publish externally” until resolved.
